verdicts.rationale: Only the hash is bound and the schema has no plaintext column.

claims.statement: OAuth grants are never admin and never submit maintenance reports; the database refuses both via a CHECK constraint.

evidence.summary: CONSTRAINT api_keys_oauth_caps CHECK (kind = 'key' OR (access <> 'admin' AND NOT maintenance_report)) makes the database refuse an OAuth grant that is admin or reports.

verdicts.rationale: CHECK constraint enforces both limits in the database.

claims.statement: Tokens and codes carry the prefixes okfat_ (access), okfrt_ (refresh), okfac_ (authorization code) and okfsc_ (sign-in code).

evidence.summary: Constants ACCESS_TOKEN_PREFIX okfat_, REFRESH_TOKEN_PREFIX okfrt_, SIGN_IN_CODE_PREFIX okfsc_, AUTHORIZATION_CODE_PREFIX okfac_.

verdicts.rationale: Constants match.

claims.statement: The server refuses to start when public_url's host is missing from allowed_hosts.

evidence.summary: validate_public_url errors when the host is not in allowed_hosts; Config loading calls validate() and maps the error (config.rs:1549); the test asserts the refusal contains 'allowed_hosts' for other.example.com. 'Refuses to start' relies on the load path returning that error, not a separate serve test.

verdicts.rationale: Validation test asserts the allowed_hosts refusal and loading validates.

claims.statement: With OAuth on, a 401 on /mcp carries WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="<public_url>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"; with OAuth off it is plain Bearer.

evidence.summary: auth.rs test asserts the 401's WWW-Authenticate equals Bearer resource_metadata=\"https://okf.example.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource\"; challenge() falls back to plain Bearer when app.oauth() is None.

verdicts.rationale: Test asserts the exact header; fallback to Bearer in challenge().

claims.statement: The OAuth routes exist only while public_url is set; without it they answer 404.

evidence.summary: OAuth::new returns None without public_url (test oauth_is_off_without_public_url), so routes are not mounted. register() also returns 404 itself when oauth is off. I did not find a test hitting /oauth/token or /oauth/authorize through the full router without public_url, so '404 for every route' is inferred from route mounting being conditional.

oauth::routes() is merged into the open router only when app.oauth().is_some(); otherwise an empty Router is used and the comment says /oauth/* and /.well-known/* stay 404. Combined with OAuth::new returning None without public_url (oauth/mod.rs:236-238, test), the routes are absent. No end-to-end test of a 404 on /oauth/token without public_url was found, but the mounting is conditional in plain code.

verdicts.rationale: Routes are mounted only with OAuth on, and OAuth is None without public_url (tested). No end-to-end 404 test.

claims.statement: Every OAuth route response carries Cache-Control: no-store, and the discovery documents also carry Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

evidence.summary: The OAuth router layer inserts Cache-Control: no-store on every response; metadata.rs sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin and its test asserts cache-control no-store for each discovery path; token.rs tests assert no-store (:688, :1197).

verdicts.rationale: Router layer and metadata tests.

claims.statement: PKCE is S256 only on every authorization; a missing or non-S256 code_challenge_method is refused.

evidence.summary: Missing/invalid code_challenge and any method other than S256 (plain, absent) yield invalid_request redirected to the client; the test asserts error=invalid_request for method plain, absent method, short challenge and absent challenge.

verdicts.rationale: Test pins plain, absent and malformed challenge refusals.

claims.statement: The resource parameter must be <public_url>/mcp: required at code exchange, optional at authorize (defaults to it), any other value refused with invalid_target.

evidence.summary: authorize treats missing resource as the default and refuses a differing one with invalid_target (test case 'https://other.example.com/mcp' -> invalid_target); token exchange does required(&form.resource) and refuses a mismatch with the stored resource; token.rs test sends a different resource and expects refusal.

verdicts.rationale: Code and tests at authorize and token endpoints.

claims.statement: A redirect URI must equal a registered one exactly, except a loopback http URI which matches on any port; scheme, host, path and query must still match.

evidence.summary: Unit tests assert loopback http URIs match on any port and that any other difference (scheme, host, path, query) does not match; authorize tests cover a portless loopback registration redirecting to another port and refusal of non-port changes.

verdicts.rationale: Unit and handler tests.

claims.statement: An authorization code works once within 60 seconds; presenting it again revokes the tokens issued from it, and a failed exchange also spends it.

evidence.summary: AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL = 60s; token.rs comment 'Each refusal below leaves the code spent'; test an_exchange_that_a_replay_overtakes_is_revoked exercises replay revocation and its comment at :778 'The code is spent by the failed attempt'.

verdicts.rationale: TTL const, spent-on-refusal behaviour and replay test.

claims.statement: A Client ID Metadata Document is fetched over https only, with no redirects, no proxy, a 5 second timeout, a 16 KiB limit, and only from public addresses unless cimd_allow_private.

evidence.summary: CIMD_TIMEOUT 5s, CIMD_MAX_BYTES 16 KiB; client built with redirect(Policy::none()), timeout, no_proxy(); tests: redirect not followed (hits==0), oversize (with and without Content-Length) refused, timeout enforced, private addresses refused by name and literal, https canonical URL required.

verdicts.rationale: Fetcher construction and tests cover each limit.

claims.statement: A CIMD document is cached for its Cache-Control max-age clamped between 5 minutes and 24 hours, and a transport-failed refetch serves the cached copy for up to 24 hours after it was fetched.

evidence.summary: CACHE_FLOOR 5 min and CACHE_CEILING 24 h clamp the max-age (test asserts max-age=999999 -> CACHE_CEILING); stale fallback on transport failure within the ceiling is tested (a_transport_failure_serves_stale_within_the_ceiling_only).

verdicts.rationale: Clamp and stale tests.

claims.statement: Dynamic client registration accepts public clients only with 1 to 10 redirect URIs (https, or http on loopback); a CIMD document lists 1 to 32.

evidence.summary: MAX_REDIRECT_URIS = 10 for registration, MAX_CIMD_REDIRECT_URIS = 32 for documents; redirect URIs must be https or http on loopback (match arm at :184-185); tests cover both caps and URI shapes.

verdicts.rationale: Caps and URI shape rules in code and tests.

claims.statement: Rate limits are: registration burst 10 then one per 6 seconds; token and revoke burst 60 then 2 per second (shared); consent form burst 20 then 1 per second; over the limit JSON endpoints answer 429 slow_down.

evidence.summary: Constants: register burst 10 at 1/6 per second, token burst 60 at 2/s, consent burst 20 at 1/s. token and revoke handlers both take from oauth.token_limit (shared bucket); over the limit they return OAuthError::SlowDown (429 slow_down, error.rs test :205). Global (not per-address) limiter objects. The per-bucket refill behaviour itself was not tested by me.

verdicts.rationale: Constants and sharing match; bucket refill not tested by me.

claims.statement: Registration is refused with 429 slow_down while 500 registered clients have no grant.

evidence.summary: MAX_UNBOUND_DCR = 500; the test fills to 500 unbound clients, accepts the 500th registration (201) and answers the next with 429 and error slow_down.

verdicts.rationale: Test asserts boundary at 500.

claims.statement: A sign-in must finish within 10 minutes of the client opening the consent page and five wrong sign-in codes end it.

evidence.summary: PENDING_TTL = 10 minutes and MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS = 5; failed_attempt ends the sign-in with 'Too many wrong sign-in codes.' once attempts reach 5 (attempts < MAX keeps the page). A test around authorize.rs:3550 imports MAX_FAILED_ATTEMPTS for the lockout.

verdicts.rationale: Constants and lockout logic match.

claims.statement: POST /oauth/revoke answers 200 for any token including an unknown one and 400 invalid_request without token; revoking an access token leaves its refresh token working; revoking a refresh token revokes its whole family.

evidence.summary: revoke returns StatusCode::OK for unknown tokens (None arm), revoke_family for a refresh token, only forgets the access token for an access one; tests revoking_a_refresh_token_revokes_its_family_and_unknown_tokens_are_fine, revoking_an_access_token_leaves_the_refresh_token and revoke_without_a_token_is_invalid_request.

verdicts.rationale: Handler and three tests.

claims.statement: OAuth JSON errors map: invalid_client 401, slow_down 429, server_error 500 (503 when Redis fails), the rest 400.

verdicts.rationale: register 404/201 and metadata test.

claims.statement: GET /healthz answers 200 when the database answers SELECT 1 within 2 seconds, otherwise 503 with database unreachable; nothing else changes the status.

evidence.summary: healthz runs SELECT 1 under HEALTH_TIMEOUT (2s); status is 200 iff reachable else 503 with database 'unreachable'. Tests: healthz_gives_up_after_its_own_deadline (503 after >= 2s with the pool exhausted) and healthz_reports_an_unreachable_database_as_503 (body asserted).

Re-audited on head: status derivation is unchanged by the new field.

claims.statement: /healthz reports redis as ok, unavailable, or null without [redis], and a Redis failure never changes the status code.

evidence.summary: redis_health returns None without redis, Some(ok) on PING success, Some(unavailable) on error or timeout; status code derives only from database reachability (:237-242). verdicts.rationale: Tests assert null, ok and unavailable with unchanged status.
Re-audited on head: the redis field and status independence are unchanged.

claims.statement: The clock check queries time_server over SNTP at startup and every 15 minutes with a 5 second limit; an offset over 2 seconds logs error 'the clock is off by more than 2 seconds', a failed query logs warn 'the clock check failed'.

evidence.summary: The first test asserts /ui/ carries content-security-policy equal to CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY plus x-content-type-options nosniff and referrer-policy no-referrer; the second asserts the policy contains `font-src 'self' https://fonts.gstatic.com;` on /ui/ and /read/. claims.statement: Passkey ceremonies wait at most 5 minutes, in memory, keyed by the okf_passkey cookie with SameSite=Strict.

claims.statement: Offline, the Account screen shows the Appearance choice and the Delete offline copies button, and leaves out the account details and Sign out.

evidence.summary: Offline, #/me shows #account-offline and the delete button works with no connection; me.js's no-session branch renders pageTitle, the 'need a connection' message, appearance() and deleteOffline() only, with no account card and no Sign out button (those exist only after the `if (!session)` return).

state.session is set only once, in boot(), from GET /session; when that read fails offline it stays unset. Nothing else in the reader assigns or clears state.session (grep: the only assignment is main.js:286), so losing the connection after an online boot leaves the session in place.

render() takes the reduced branch (Appearance and Delete offline copies only) only when ctx.state.session is absent; with a session it renders the account card, session expiry and Sign out whatever the connection. Sign out offline then shows 'The server could not be reached to end the session.' So after an online boot followed by loss of connection, Account shows the details and Sign out, contrary to the unconditional "Offline it shows..." in reader.md:70-72. The cited ui_e2e test covers only offline at boot.

verdicts.rationale: Offline journeys reach the account-offline view and the delete button works there; the no-session branch of me.js omits the details and Sign out and includes Appearance.

The reduced Account view depends on state.session being absent, which happens only when the reader boots offline; the session is never re-read or cleared, so a reader that loses its connection after an online boot still shows the account details and Sign out. The earlier supported verdict rested on a test of the offline-at-boot case only (raised in review on PR #901). Fix: either qualify docs/reference/reader.md:70-72 to "When the reader starts offline, Account shows..." or change src/http/read/js/screens/me.js to take the reduced branch whenever the server cannot be reached (e.g. re-read /session on opening Account), with a ui_e2e test that goes offline after an online boot.

claims.statement: A provisioner key opens at most 50 provisioner audit entries per clock hour; further new kinds count in one overflow entry per action (target '*'), and an entry already opened keeps counting in its own entry.
claims.source: Issue #423 decision: 'Rate-limit the writes so a scripted flood can't fill the audit table'; PR body 'a key opens at most 50 entries an hour, the rest count in one overflow entry per action'

evidence.summary: A bucket not yet in audit_access_counts counts against a per-key-hour 'provcap' row; when used exceeds 50 the bucket becomes 'provov' (one per action), target '*', matched None, details {overflow}. A known bucket skips the budget so it keeps counting. Bounds: 50 regular entries per key-hour (shared by both actions) plus at most 2 overflow entries, so up to 52 rows per key-hour, which the PR text ('at most 50 entries... the rest in one overflow entry per action') does not state exactly. The unit test sends 57 routes and asserts 50 entries plus one overflow with count 7, route-0 counting 2, and lookups overflowing into their own '*' entry with count 3. A concurrent double-count of one new bucket only over-spends the budget, never under-enforces it.

evidence.locator: src/store/audit.rs:1371-1401 (cap logic), 1206; test a_key_opens_a_bounded_number_of_entries... at ~3264-3300 (read, not run)
evidence.summary: At HEAD a bucket that does not exist counts against a per-key-hour 'provcap' row; when used exceeds PROVISIONER_ENTRIES_PER_HOUR (50) it becomes a 'provov' bucket (one per action), target '*', matched None, details {overflow}. An existing bucket skips the budget and keeps counting. Bound: 50 regular entries per key-hour shared by both actions plus up to 2 overflow entries (one per action), so up to 52 rows; the claim and docs state this as 'one overflow entry per action'. The test checks 50 routes plus one overflow with count 7, route-0 count 2, and 3 lookups overflowing into their own '*' entry. Read only; not run.

verdicts.rationale: The budget is enforced in record_provisioner_use and tested with 57 routes. The budget is 50 regular entries across both actions plus up to two overflow entries (52 rows per key-hour); the PR and docs state the overflow rule, so this is exact but worth knowing.

claims.statement: The cause of snapshot_build_documents_are_children_of_the_build_span reading left 0 right 3000 is a tracing-core callsite-interest race: while only one dispatcher is registered, a thread reaching a callsite for the first time computes and caches its interest from its own default subscriber, so a thread with no subscriber caches the callsite as never although another test's scoped subscriber is live.
claims.source: issue #481 req 1 'confirming the cause first'; PR body: 'Cause of the caller test's left: 0, right: 3000 (confirmed in tracing-core 0.1.36, callsite.rs)'

evidence.summary: register_dispatch sets has_just_one = (registered dispatchers <= 1); rebuilder() returns JustOne when true, and JustOne::for_each calls dispatcher::get_default only, i.e. the registering thread's own default subscriber; no default gives Interest::never (rebuild_callsite_interest unwrap_or_else(never)). The result is cached on the callsite and only recomputed when a dispatch registers or rebuild_interest_cache runs. This matches the stated mechanism.

claims.statement: run() in src/shared/announce.rs emits a tracing info event on every SubscriptionEvent::Subscribed, carrying resubscribe (false for the loop's first Subscribed, true afterwards) and disconnected_ms.
claims.source: Issue #592: 'log at info on (re)subscribe'; PR body: 'info on every Subscribed, with resubscribe (false for the first) and disconnected_ms after a loss.'

evidence.summary: info is emitted on every Subscribed with resubscribe=subscribed_before and disconnected_ms, but `let mut subscribed_before = false` (and disconnected_at) is declared inside the `Ok(mut subscription)` arm, so it resets for every fresh subscription: the first Subscribed after a grace replacement, stream end or failed subscribe logs resubscribe=false and no disconnected_ms, though it is a resubscribe. The comment says 'this loop'; the docs say 'resubscribe is true after the first'.

The test only scripts Subscribed events inside attempt 1 (Subscribed, Disconnected, Subscribed), so it asserts resubscribe=true once within one subscription. Attempts 2-4 never emit Subscribed, so no case checks the first Subscribed of a replaced subscription, where the code logs resubscribe=false.

`subscribed_before` is now declared above the `while` loop (line 444) and set after each info line, so only the loop's first Subscribed logs resubscribe=false, including across replaced subscriptions. disconnected_at stays per subscription, which the docs now state.

Attempt 4 now emits Subscribed in a fresh subscription after a grace replacement and a failed subscribe; the test asserts 3 info lines and 2 with resubscribe=true, so a flag reset per subscription would give 1 and fail.

verdicts.rationale: info is logged on every Subscribed, but resubscribe and disconnected_ms are tracked per subscription, not per loop, so after a grace replacement, stream end or failed subscribe the first Subscribed of the new subscription reports resubscribe=false. That is the exact (re)subscribe case operators need to see, and the test does not script it. Fix: move `subscribed_before` out of the `Ok(subscription)` arm to just above the `while` loop (and keep the loss start time across a replacement so disconnected_ms covers the whole outage), then extend the log test so a Subscribed after a grace replacement asserts resubscribe=true.
Flag now lives across subscriptions and the test covers a Subscribed after a replaced subscription.

refresh_to awaits the lock with no connection in hand; its load closure (build(pool, ...)) acquires one only after the lock is held, which is the lock-then-connection order the coordinator allowed.

claims.statement: A replica that lost the CatalogMeta message misses a new catalog only until the absent entry's 5 s TTL (ABSENT_TTL) expires, or a resubscribe's catch-up (App::catch_up_catalogs) marks directory rows stale.
claims.source: Changelog: "A replica misses a new catalog only if it lost the message (then until the absent entry's 5 s TTL, or a resubscribe's catch-up, `App::catch_up_catalogs`)."

evidence.summary: ABSENT_TTL = 5 s; catch_up_catalogs calls directory.mark_all_stale() (rows stale, read again on next use). Note: catch-up marks rows stale; whether it also clears absent entries was not checked, but the claim's catch-up half concerns row staleness.
mark_all_stale marks every row stale AND invalidates every absent entry ("no absence is trusted"), so catch-up covers absent names as well.

verdicts.rationale: ABSENT_TTL is 5 s; catch_up_catalogs -> mark_all_stale stales rows and clears absent entries.

claims.statement: Issue #675 is resolved: watchdog.sh's ps scans are time-bounded, a hung scan is a skipped pass, and a test covers it.
claims.source: https://github.com/hypotheosis/okf_mcp/issues/675

evidence.summary: Children cover the bounded scans, skip semantics, the stub-ps test, command-line secrecy, test run, unbounded-call survey and README; all supported.

verdicts.rationale: All seven children supported; together they cover bounding, skip semantics, test, and secrecy.

claims.statement: Each of watchdog.sh's three main ps -eo scans (process list for expectations, test/gate processes, idle readers) runs through agentic_bounded_call and its output is captured to a variable that the loops then read.
claims.source: Issue #675: run watchdog.sh's ps scan through agentic_bounded_call (capture to a variable, then loop); PR: "runs each of its three `ps -eo ...` scans through `agentic_bounded_call`"

evidence.summary: scan_ps runs agentic_bounded_call ps and stores output via printf -v. Three scans use it: procs (line 123, check_expectations), all_procs and readers (line 174); loops read them by here-string. No unbounded ps -eo remains (the other two ps calls, lines 187/214, are also bounded).

Every ps invocation in watchdog.sh sits behind agentic_bounded_call; only scan_ps's own ps -eo lines are arguments to scan_ps. Mutation check: replacing the bounded call with plain ps makes the two new tests fail.

verdicts.rationale: Code shows all three scans via scan_ps/agentic_bounded_call, captured then looped; mutation shows the bound is what the tests exercise.

claims.statement: When a ps scan times out or fails, watchdog.sh prints a warning on stderr, skips that pass without an alarm (no WATCHDOG output, no exit 3) and does not exit in looping mode; with --once it exits 0.
claims.source: Issue #675: a timed-out scan is a skipped pass with a warning, not an alarm and not an exit; PR: "A scan that times out or fails skips that pass with a warning; it is not an alarm and does not exit."

evidence.summary: Both ok (3106 ms, 1113 ms). Loop test: exit 124 from timeout (still running), warning present at least twice, no WATCHDOG output. --once: exit 0, warning, no WATCHDOG.

scan_ps warns to stderr and returns 1; the main loop then exits 0 only if --once, else sleeps and continues (before any WATCHDOG echo/exit 3); check_expectations returns 0 on a failed scan. Skip never reaches found/alarm.

A stub ps that finds an over-limit process in the first scan and hangs only the third scan gives a warning, no WATCHDOG alert, exit 0 with --once and a still-running loop. Both tests fail against the previous watchdog.sh and pass now (82 passed, 3 runs in a row).

verdicts.rationale: Tests run both modes against a hanging ps and pass; control flow confirms skip is before any alarm or exit 3.
A failing scan skips the pass even after an earlier scan found an alert; tested for --once and the loop.

claims.statement: tools/agentic/tests/run.sh has cases using a stub ps that sleeps past the bound: the looping watchdog keeps running and warns on at least two passes, and --once exits 0; both fail when the scan is unbounded.
claims.source: Issue #675: add a tools/agentic/tests/run.sh case with a stub ps that sleeps past the bound; PR: "With the old unbounded scan restored, both fail."

evidence.locator: bash tools/agentic/tests/run.sh (both ps_scan_hangs tests ok); mutation in scratch copy replacing agentic_bounded_call ps with ps
evidence.summary: Stub ps is `exec sleep 30` first on PATH with AGENTIC_CALL_TIMEOUT=1. Assertions read: rc 124, warning text, no WATCHDOG, warning count >= 2; once: rc 0. With the unbounded call restored in a scratch copy, run.sh reported 78 passed, 2 failed, exactly these two.

verdicts.rationale: Tests exist with the stated assertions and both fail (2 of 80) when the unbounded ps is restored.

claims.statement: The watchdog never prints or logs process command lines (ps args= output), including in the new timeout warning.
claims.source: Brief for #675: the watchdog must never print or log process command lines; PR: "A timed-out scan prints a warning on stderr without any scan output."

evidence.summary: The scan_ps warning prints only a fixed text and the numeric status; captured output is discarded on failure. found+= lines carry only pid, elapsed, comm, cwd. $args is used only inside case/grep matching, never echoed. lib.sh's leftover-process warning prints '$2', the command name (ps), not its arguments. ps stderr is not captured but ps does not print command lines in errors. Tests also assert no WATCHDOG output on a hung scan.

evidence.locator: gap: no test asserts a command-line sentinel is absent from the warning
evidence.summary: The tests check only for WATCHDOG and the warning text. Nothing asserts that a unique token placed in the stub ps's args or output never reaches stdout/stderr. Support rests on code reading alone.

verdicts.rationale: No path echoes ps args or scan output; the warning is fixed text plus a status number. Caveat (neutral EVD-0886): no test pins this with a sentinel in the stub's args.

claims.statement: Among process-table commands (ps, pgrep) in tools/agentic/*.sh, apart from the watchdog's ps scans the only unbounded one is pgrep -c -g in lib.sh:56. Local reads such as readlink and getconf in watchdog.sh were not part of the survey.
claims.source: PR: "Other unbounded external calls in `tools/agentic/*.sh`: only `pgrep -c -g` in `lib.sh`"

evidence.summary: The only non-watchdog pgrep/ps in the scripts is lib.sh:56 pgrep -c -g (unbounded). Remaining watchdog calls are bounded (ps, find, git) or local builtins/coreutils (readlink on /proc, date, tr, awk, grep, read of /proc files). A readlink or read on a stuck /proc entry is theoretically unbounded but is not an external-tool call of the kind meant.

Re-run after the review fix: every ps in watchdog.sh goes through scan_ps or agentic_bounded_call; the only other process-table command is the unbounded pgrep -c -g at lib.sh:56. readlink and getconf are local reads, outside the narrowed claim.

verdicts.rationale: Grep of all tools/agentic scripts finds only lib.sh:56 pgrep unbounded outside the now-bounded ps scans.
The narrowed statement holds: only lib.sh:56 pgrep is an unbounded process-table command outside the bounded scans.
